Extract layer styles from a QGIS project file

Source: R/gq_qgs_extract.R
gq_qgs_extract.Rd

Parses a .qgs project, or a .qlr layer definition file, and extracts symbology (fill, stroke, casing, overlay, classification, labels) for all vector layers into a list suitable for writing to registry.json. Both formats keep their layers as <maplayer> nodes, so one reader serves both.

Usage

gq_qgs_extract(path)

Arguments

path

Path to a .qgs or .qlr file.

Value

A list with name, version, source, and layers elements. Each layer contains type, source_layer, fill/stroke/casing/overlay/ classification/label as applicable, and a note naming any symbol layer or renderer it does not model.

Details

The registry models what tmap and mapgl can render, not every property QGIS stores. A symbol layer it cannot express (a pattern fill, a stacked marker) and a renderer it does not read are named in the layer's note. Cap and join style and symbol-layer pass order are not read and not noted. The QML from gq_style_qml() carries all of it losslessly.

Labels carry the label column as field, or the raw QGIS expression as expression when the label is computed (concat(...), CASE ...), never both, so a consumer reading field as a column cannot be handed an expression. placement is QGIS's placement mode as a word ("line", "around_point", ...). merge_lines and min_feature_size (mm) are hints for the consumer's data prep: QGIS joins connected lines that share a label and skips short features, which tmap and MapLibre cannot do, so dissolve by the label field and drop short features before drawing.

A symbol's opacity and the layer's own (<layerOpacity>) are folded into every opacity the layer emits, as QGIS composes them.

A label's size is recorded in points and its halo width in millimetres, converted from QGIS's millimetres or inches where the project uses them. A size in pixels, map units or a percentage has no fixed print size, so it is left out and the label's note says so.

Examples

path <- system.file("examples", "mini_project.qgs", package = "gq")
reg <- gq_qgs_extract(path)

# Shows all layers extracted from the QGIS project
names(reg$layers)
#> [1] "lakes"     "streams"   "crossings" "roads"    

# Polygon layer — fill and stroke extracted from SimpleFill symbol
reg$layers$lakes
#> $type
#> [1] "polygon"
#> 
#> $source_layer
#> [1] "lakes"
#> 
#> $fill
#> $fill$color
#> [1] "#c6ddf0"
#> 
#> $fill$opacity
#> [1] 0.851
#> 
#> 
#> $stroke
#> $stroke$color
#> [1] "#7ba7cc"
#> 
#> $stroke$width
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> 

# Categorized layer — classification field and per-class colors
reg$layers$roads$classification
#> $field
#> [1] "road_type"
#> 
#> $classes
#> $classes$highway
#> $classes$highway$color
#> [1] "#c0392b"
#> 
#> $classes$highway$width
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $classes$highway$label
#> [1] "Highway"
#> 
#> 
#> $classes$arterial
#> $classes$arterial$color
#> [1] "#e67e22"
#> 
#> $classes$arterial$width
#> [1] 1.5
#> 
#> $classes$arterial$label
#> [1] "Arterial"
#> 
#> 
#> 

# Labels — field, font, size, weight, halo all captured
reg$layers$roads$label
#> $field
#> [1] "road_name"
#> 
#> $font
#> [1] "Arial"
#> 
#> $size
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $weight
#> [1] "bold"
#> 
#> $color
#> [1] "#1a3c5e"
#> 
#> $halo
#> $halo$color
#> [1] "#ffffff"
#> 
#> $halo$width
#> [1] 1.5
#> 
#>
